sections.label: Reliance on imported natural gas
sections.summary: Over 95% of electricity is generated from natural gas, up from 77% in 2010.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Our reliance on imported natural gas has grown, with over 95% of our electricity generated from natural gas, up from 77% in 2010.

sections.label: Proposed Gas Act updates
sections.summary: MTI and EMA propose updating the Gas Act in four key areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and the Energy Market Authority (EMA) are, therefore, proposing to update the Gas Act in four key areas: first, to enhance gas supply security and the regulation of safety of gas-related activities; second, to enhance protection of critical gas infrastructure and deterrence for serious offences; third, to facilitate competition in the gas market; and fourth, to clarify and improve procedural and technical provisions in the Gas Act.

sections.label: Directions during severe gas shortage
sections.summary: Clause 14 lets EMA, with the Minister's approval, issue directions during a severe gas shortage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The first amendment, in clause 14 of the Bill, introduces a new part VIIIA to the Gas Act, where in the event of an imminent or actual severe gas shortage, EMA, with the Minister's approval, is empowered to issue directions to require any person to take measures specified by EMA to address or alleviate the severe gas shortage, or prevent it from occurring or continuing.

sections.label: Designated gas licensees
sections.summary: The LNG terminal operator is added as a designated gas licensee alongside existing ones.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Presently, the only designated gas licensees are the gas transporter licensee, that is PowerGas Ltd, which is responsible for the operation of the gas transmission system, and its agent licensee, that is, SP PowerGrid Ltd.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: We are including the LNG terminal operator, that is, Singapore LNG Corporation Pte Ltd, as a "designated gas licensee", in view of its critical role in ensuring energy security.

sections.label: Licensees applying for judicial management
sections.summary: Clause 22 lets licensees apply for a Judicial Management order after obtaining EMA's consent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The fifth amendment, also in clause 22 of the Bill, amends section 34(6)(b) of the Gas Act to allow licensees to apply for a Judicial Management (JM) order under Part VIIIA of the Companies Act once EMA's consent is obtained.

sections.label: Offence of damaging submarine pipelines
sections.summary: Clause 6 makes it an offence to damage any submarine gas pipeline.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The sixth amendment, in clause 6 of the Bill, introduces a new section 32B to the Gas Act that makes it an offence to damage any submarine gas pipeline.

sections.label: Higher fines for submarine pipeline damage
sections.summary: Repairing submarine gas pipelines costs more than land-based ones, so a higher maximum fine of $2 million and/or up to five years' imprisonment applies on conviction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: In view of the higher costs of repairing submarine gas pipelines vis-à-vis land-based gas pipelines, a higher maximum fine of $2 million and/or imprisonment of up to five years upon conviction will be imposed.

sections.label: Additional fine for dishonest gas consumption
sections.summary: Clause 7 amends section 47 of the Gas Act to mandate an additional fine of three times the value of gas dishonestly consumed for dishonest consumption and meter tampering offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: However, in cases where the dishonest consumption of gas is carried out on a large scale and the value of gas dishonestly consumed is substantial, the existing penalty can be disproportionately low compared to the value of gas consumed and ineffective as deterrence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Hence, the eighth amendment, also in clause 7 of the Bill, amends section 47 of the Gas Act to mandate that the Court imposes an additional fine equivalent to three times the value of gas dishonestly consumed, on conviction for dishonest consumption of gas and meter tampering offences.

sections.label: EMA functions, pipeline conversion, cost recovery
sections.summary: Clauses 3 and 21 clarify EMA's regulatory functions, broaden regulations on converting gas pipeline networks, and let EMA recover costs for services without prescribing them as fees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Second, to better reflect EMA’s functions in ensuring the security and reliability of our gas supply, clause 3 of the Bill amends section 3 of the Gas Act to clarify that EMA’s regulatory functions include arranging for the secure operation of the gas transmission system, which EMA already performs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Third, clause 21 of the Bill amends section 96 of the Gas Act to broaden regulations that may be made under section 96(2)(o) relating to the conversion of a gas pipeline network to convey natural gas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The broadened regulations will enable EMA to require relevant parties, such as building owners or managers, to submit updated plans and other information to the licensees carrying out the conversion works.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: It will also allow regulations to be made to provide for termination of supply of gas to any premises if the conversion is not carried out successfully, on safety or other grounds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Clause 21 also amends section 96 to enable EMA to recover costs for services provided in connection with its regulatory functions, without having to prescribe the costs as fees.

sections.label: Imported gas share of energy generation
sections.summary: Imported natural gas account for 95% of Singapore's energy generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Imported natural gas account for 95% of our energy generation.

sections.label: Reduced dependence on piped natural gas
sections.summary: Singapore has long piped gas from Malaysia and Indonesia, dependence fell from 100% to 77%, and the six PNG contracts expire between this year and 2029.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All this while, Singapore has been buying gas and piping it from Malaysia and Indonesia through our strong bilateral relationship, and we have enjoyed this facility for a very long time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That dependence has been reduced over the years from 100% to 77%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is an important step in reducing our reliance on PNG and I would like to congratulate the executives for their far-sightedness to build the terminal to strengthen our energy security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And, from what I understand, the existing six contracts for PNG from our neighbours will expire between this year and 2029.

sections.label: September blackout affecting customers
sections.summary: On 18 September, about two weeks ago, a major blackout affected over 146,000 residential and commercial customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: About two weeks ago on 18 September, we faced a major blackout that affected over 146,000 residential and commercial customers.

sections.label: LNG terminal and gas sources
sections.summary: The Government built an LNG terminal, enabling natural gas procurement as LNG from sources including Australia, the US and Trinidad and Tobago.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: To that end, the Government has built an LNG terminal, which has enabled us to procure natural gas in the form of LNG from a wider range of sources, such as Australia, the United States (US) as well as Trinidad and Tobago.

sections.label: Terminal peak throughput capacity
sections.summary: The terminal has a peak throughput capacity of 11 million tonnes per annum, sufficient for near-future demand.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: The terminal today has a peak throughput capacity of 11 million tonnes per annum, sufficient to meet demand for the near future.

sections.label: LNG trading companies in Singapore
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore's efforts built an LNG trading community, with more than 45 companies having an LNG trading or business development presence here.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Thanks to the efforts of Enterprise Singapore in building the LNG trading community, there are now more than 45 companies with an LNG trading or business development presence here.

sections.label: Hospital backup power supply
sections.summary: Public hospitals have dual supply sources and backup power systems like diesel generators and UPS, which activated during the 18 September outage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: As for our public hospitals, these are provided with dual supply sources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: So, if one of the supply sources fails, each is able to provide backup to the hospital.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: In addition, if there is any disruption from the main power source, there are backup power systems, such as diesel generators and Uninterrupted Power Supplies (UPS) systems, and these will automatically kick in to support critical equipment and critical facilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: During the power outage on 18 September, hospitals in the affected areas activated their backup power supply immediately, and this prevented disruptions to their operations and patient care.
